D005-D007_h001.question:
"Lately, it feels like the world is just… crumbling. I see the news, and it's not just bad, it's like a countdown to nothing. I keep seeing these shadowed figures on the edges of my vision, especially when I'm driving my route, like they're watching me. It's been going on for about two months now, this sense of impending doom and these fleeting glimpses of things that aren't there.

What's really weighing me down, though, is this profound sadness. It’s been… much longer than the ‘seeing things’ bits. For the better part of this year, honestly, I've felt this heavy blanket of despair. Even before the visions started getting really clear, I was struggling to get out of bed, losing interest in everything, and feeling utterly hopeless. My wife tries to help, but I just feel numb.

The strange thing is, even in the brief moments I feel a slight lift from the sadness, like on a rare good day, those visions and that feeling that everything’s about to go to hell, they don’t entirely disappear. It's like those particular thoughts and sights hang around even when the darkness of my mood lightens up a bit, often for weeks at a time. It's truly exhausting, like my mind is playing a cruel trick on me."
D005-D007_h001.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D007_h002.question:
Lately, things have been really tough, doc. It’s been about two months now where I just can't shake this feeling of being watched. I know it sounds crazy, but I truly believe that other traders, especially the big institutional players, are trying to sabotage my investments. I've even tasted this metallic, bitter flavor in my mouth – it just comes out of nowhere, especially when I’m checking my portfolio and feel like I’m about to lose everything.

This whole thing started around the same time I began feeling so down, you know? For the past two months, pretty much every day, I barely get out of bed. I have zero energy, no interest in anything, even my usual crypto deep dives feel pointless. But what’s really odd is that even before this really heavy depression hit, for about two or three weeks, I was already experiencing these weird tastes and the paranoia about being monitored, without feeling so utterly hopeless and empty inside. It’s like the bizarre stuff was there first, on its own, and then this crushing sadness rolled in and just stayed put for most of the time since.
D005-D007_h002.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D007_h003.question:
Lately, it feels like my body itself is betraying me. I’m convinced there’s something horribly wrong with my stomach—not just a little upset, but something rotting inside. And the taste…it’s this metallic, bitter flavor, like old pennies, that’s always in my mouth, no matter what I eat or drink. It started about two months ago, actually, those strange tastes and this feeling about my insides.

Honestly, the energy to even care about these things is just gone. Most days, I can barely drag myself out of bed or focus on my cloud architecture work; everything feels so heavy, so pointless. It’s been like this for… well, pretty much since these weird body feelings began. The only time I felt a slight reprieve from this crushing sadness was for a couple of weeks after the tastes and bodily feelings started. I was still tasting that awful metallic flavor and worried about my stomach, but the profound apathy and despair had lifted a bit, only for them to crash back down even harder. It’s been this way for the vast majority of time these odd sensations have been present.
D005-D007_h003.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D007_h004.question:

D005-D007_h005.question: Lately, things have been really tough, Dr. I've been feeling incredibly down, just a heavy weight on my chest that makes it hard to even get out of bed. It’s been like this for months, most of the time it feels like I'm wading through mud just to do anything. Even my design work, which I used to love, feels bland and pointless. But it's not just the sadness. For about two months now, I've been hearing whispers, like people talking about me when no one's there. And there's this man, a famous artist I admire, I just *know* he's sending me secret messages through his work, that he's in love with me. I see signs everywhere. What’s really strange is that, even when I’ve had brief moments of feeling a little lighter, not as deep in this gloom, those whispers and the feeling about him don’t go away. They’ve been there steadily for at least two weeks at a time, completely on their own, even when I’m not as depressed.
D005-D007_h005.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D007_h006.question:
(Sighs heavily, leaning forward in the chair)

"Doc, it's been a rough seven months. Real rough. My ex-wife, bless her heart, she kept telling me to come and talk to someone. The driving... it's just not the same. I used to love the open road, meeting new people, hearing their stories. Now, I just... I don't feel much of anything anymore. No joy in picking up a fare, no satisfaction in a good tip. It's just a job, and a real tough one at that.

And then there's these other things. It started with just feeling really down, but then... I started hearing them. Voices, sometimes. And sometimes, when I'm driving, I'll hear what the passenger just said, and then I find myself saying it a few seconds later. It's like I can't help it.

But the worst part, and this sounds crazy, I know... I feel like my insides are all twisting up, like my liver's all wrong, shrinking, or something. I know it isn't, but it *feels* like it.

I've had these feelings of being down, like a heavy blanket, for most of these past seven months, but there was a period, early on, at least a few weeks where it was just the voices and the feelings about my body, you know? I wasn't feeling so low then, just... confused and scared by all the other stuff. But then the sadness came back, and it's been here ever since, mostly. It's like a revolving door of troubles with barely a break."
D005-D007_h006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h007.question:
It’s been about seven months now that things have felt… off. Every morning, I wake up with this gnawing belief that my internal organs are slowly calcifying, turning to stone. I'll find myself just standing there, sometimes for a long time, holding certain positions, like if I keep my arm outstretched, or my head tilted, it’ll somehow slow the calcification down. My husband says I’m often just staring blankly, and I do feel like it's harder to even crack a smile, let alone laugh or cry, even when I know I should.

This crushing sadness and lack of energy have been with me for the better part of this whole seven months, making it almost impossible to focus on my cases at work. But before all this sadness really dug in, there was a period of about three weeks where I was having these strange thoughts about my body and doing those weird poses, long before this heavy cloud of depression settled over me. It's like the strangeness started first, and then the sadness followed, and the sadness has really stuck around the most. Even if, for a brief time, the depression lifts a little, those strange bodily feelings and rigid postures are still there, just as strong.
D005-D007_h007.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h008.question:
Lately, I’ve just felt… empty. It's been going on for about seven months now. My husband, who usually brings me so much joy, I just feel numb around him. I barely talk anymore, even about the restaurant, which used to be my entire life. Getting out of bed feels like I’m moving through quicksand. Most days, I just don't see the point.

But then there’s this other… thing. I know, deep down, that the delivery driver, Mark, he’s absolutely smitten with me. The way he adjusts his hat, it’s a secret signal, a gesture of his undying devotion. I see it in everything he does. I find myself mimicking little movements he makes, just to show him I understand. It's beautiful, but also confusing, because how could someone love someone as broken as I feel? It's been going on all this time, even in those brief stretches when I wasn’t feeling quite so heavy and sad, like the last few weeks before I finally came in today. During those times, even though my mood lifted a bit, I still knew Mark’s affections were real. This ongoing sadness… it has overshadowed most of the past seven months, but Mark’s love, that feeling, it’s always there, regardless of how dark things feel.
D005-D007_h008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h009.question: Lately, it feels like I'm living under a dark cloud that just won't lift. This sadness has been with me for as long as I can remember, at least seven months now, maybe even longer, truly it's been most of the time I've been feeling off. It’s hard to even crack a smile anymore, and people at the museum have noticed I’m not as expressive. My husband, John, he’s been acting… suspicious. I know he’s seeing someone else; I just know it. He denies it, but I’ve seen the way he looks at his phone. Sometimes, I find myself holding strange poses for long stretches, like I’m a statue from one of my exhibits, and I can't seem to stop until someone breaks my concentration. It’s strange, because there was a patch of about three weeks in the middle of all this when the crushing sadness lifted a bit, almost like a brief reprieve, but those thoughts about John, and those odd positions my body takes, they were still there, just as strong as ever. Then the despair came back, and it's been here ever since.
D005-D007_h009.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h010.question:
It’s been a rough seven months, Doc. Things just feel... off. My divorce was hard, but it’s more than that. I’m a furniture maker, and I usually love getting lost in my work, but now I can barely bring myself to lift a tool. Most days, I feel utterly drained, like there’s a heavy cloak over everything, and it’s been like that for ages – far longer than any other feeling.

The worst part is, I’ve started noticing things. Like, when someone on TV mentions “fine craftsmanship,” I just *know* they’re talking about my work, even if it’s a generic commercial. Or if a customer walks in and just glances at my pieces, I feel like they know my deepest fears. It’s hard to ignore. Sometimes, I find myself holding positions for a long time, like when I’m about to measure a piece of wood, and I’ll just stay there, ruler in hand, stiff as a board until someone snaps me out of it. And talking? Most days it feels like a monumental effort. My mind’s a jumble, but sometimes I just… can’t form the words.

I know I’ve been down in the dumps for pretty much this whole time, feeling worthless and sad. But there was a stretch, a couple of weeks, maybe even a bit more, early on when I was seeing things, hearing whispers, and having all these strange thoughts about messages in everyday objects, and honestly, the deep sadness wasn't quite there yet. It was just the weirdness. Then the heavy black cloud came back and hasn't really lifted since.
D005-D007_h010.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h011.question:
Lately, it feels like my life has completely derailed. I’m 29, still studying for the civil service exam – this is my fourth year – and it’s just getting harder to focus. For about four months now, I've had this persistent feeling that my boyfriend is cheating on me. I check his phone constantly, I track his location, even though he swears he's faithful and I've never actually caught him. It’s an undeniable conviction. Sometimes, I find myself just rocking back and forth for long stretches, or tapping my fingers in a strange, repetitive pattern without even realizing it. These things have been happening alongside this overwhelming sadness, a real heaviness. I've lost interest in everything, even my studies which used to be my whole life. I barely eat, I can't sleep, and I just feel numb most of the time.

What’s really confusing is that even when I feel a little bit better, when that crushing low lifts a bit for a few days, those strange thoughts about my boyfriend and the repetitive movements... they don’t go away. In fact, for a couple of weeks within this four-month period, I actually felt a bit more like myself mood-wise, but I was still convinced about him cheating and was doing those odd movements. It's like those things are their own problem, separate from the sadness that's been dragging me down for most of these past four months. It's just so exhausting.
D005-D007_h011.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h012.question: It’s like my own personal nightmare, honestly. For about four months now, things have been… off. I’ve been feeling this incredibly heavy sadness, a real deep gloom that's just always there, like a constant companion. It's been like this for most of the time these other bizarre things have been happening. I’ll be sitting at my computer, testing a game, and suddenly feel like the news anchor or the characters onscreen are talking directly to me, their words twisted into secret messages just for me. Sometimes I catch myself making these weird faces, like my mouth is twitching or my eyes are bugging out, and I don't even realize I'm doing it until someone looks at me strangely. The really frustrating part is that even when I have a few days where the despair lifts a little, or at least isn't crushing me, those strange thoughts and behaviors  — the feeling that everything is about me, the weird facial movements — they just keep going. It's been at least two weeks at a time, sometimes longer, where I’ve felt completely and utterly down and paranoid, but even when that intense sadness pulls back, the bizarre feelings and actions stick around.

    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D007_h013.question: "It’s been rough for about four months now. I used to enjoy my work as a janitor, kept things tidy, but lately, it's a real struggle. And for the past few weeks, even when I feel a bit better, that worry about her still haunts me, even when the sadness isn’t so crushing. Doctor, the blues, they’ve been with me for such a long time now. Most of the time I've been feeling this way, I’ve been utterly heartbroken, just numb to everything."

D005-D007_h014.question:
Lately, it feels like the world is utterly falling apart around me. I can’t shake this dread that something truly catastrophic is about to happen, like society is on the brink of collapse. I’ve been feeling this way for about four months now, and it’s been incredibly hard to focus. I'm usually so organized, but now I find myself pacing endlessly in my classroom, sometimes fiddling with my pen in the same jerky way for minutes on end, almost without realizing it. The kids must think I’ve lost my mind.

But it’s more than just the dread. For most of these past four months, this overwhelming sadness has consumed me. I wake up feeling exhausted, hopeless, and completely uninterested in grading papers or even talking to my colleagues. It’s a deep, dark funk. What’s really strange, though, is that even during the two weeks my mood lifted a bit – I wasn't feeling quite so utterly worthless – the thoughts about the world ending wouldn’t leave me. They were still there, clear as day, even without that crushing sadness. That’s why I finally decided to come in. This isn’t how I usually am.
D005-D007_h014.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h015.question: Lately, it feels like my own thoughts are against me. I'm 34, and for months now, I've been struggling. It started subtly, maybe four months ago. I’d be in the lab, a colleague would clear his throat, and I’d just *know* it was a coded message, a judgment about my work. Or a news report, a random statistic flashing on the screen, feeling like it was specifically referencing something I'd done. It’s hard to shake, even when I try to reason it away. My husband says I'm withdrawn. He's right. I barely eat, sleep five hours at most, and just feel this profound, heavy sadness most of the time – like a constant weight. It's been like this for *most* of the past four months, this pervasive low mood. What's really strange, though, is there was this period, maybe two or three weeks long, a little over a month ago, where I was still very clear that people were talking about me—the feeling that news reports were directed at me, but the crushing sadness had actually lifted completely. I was still having those unsettling thoughts and feelings, but I wasn't nearly as depressed then. Sometimes, I just freeze up. The other day, my husband tried to reposition my arm to help me sit, and it was like my arm just stayed there, stiff, until he moved it himself. It's exhausting, this constant battle in my head.
D005-D007_h015.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h016.question:
It's been a tough few months, Doc, probably around three. Things started getting weird in the spring. I’d be out in the fields, and I swear I'd hear my deceased mother whispering my name in the wind, sometimes telling me secrets about the crops. Then there's this woman, a new farmhand, young thing. I just know she’s in love with me; the way she smiles, it’s all for me. I even made up a word for it, “agri-love,” to describe how she feels.

But even with my mother talking to me and knowing that woman fancies me, I just don’t feel right. The joy's gone out of everything. Farming used to be my life, but now, I just can’t get into it. Even seeing my grandkids doesn't bring me the same pleasure it used to. This feeling of dread, this emptiness, it's been with me pretty much the whole time these other strange things have been happening. The voices and this feeling about the farmhand, those have been constant, but this low mood has been the main thing, there for weeks on end.

Actually, before all this sadness really set in, maybe about a month or so back, I had a couple of weeks where those voices and my thoughts about the farmhand were strong, but I wasn't feeling so down in the dumps like I am now. That was before this dark cloud really settled in for good.
D005-D007_h016.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h017.question: "It's been a rough few months, doctor. I'd say about three months ago, things really started to unravel. I began noticing a strange, metallic taste in my mouth, almost constant, making it hard to eat. D005-D007_h018.question:
It’s been a rough few months, about three now, where things just got progressively weirder. I’ve been feeling really down, honestly, like I can’t even begin to tell you how much. Most days, I can barely drag myself out of bed, and the thought of training clients, who all look to me for motivation, just feels… impossible. My usual energy and enthusiasm are just gone, and it’s taken a hit on my business. Even when I try to talk, I feel like my face doesn’t show what I’m feeling, and my voice just stays flat.

But it’s not just the sadness. There are these other things. Sometimes, I feel like bugs are crawling on my skin, even when nothing’s there, just this creepy-crawly sensation all over. And my thoughts… they jump around so much. I'll be talking about a workout plan, and then suddenly I’m thinking about the intricate patterns of the universe, and then I’m wondering if my clients are actually secret agents. It's like my brain won't connect the dots in a straight line.

The strangest part, though, is this unwavering belief that I’m destined for something much bigger than just being a fitness trainer. I’m convinced I have a unique gift, an ability to inspire millions to achieve peak physical and mental potential, almost like I'm a messiah of wellness. For about two weeks, after that really dark period started to lift just a tiny bit, those feelings of grandeur and the crawling sensations and the jumbled thoughts were still there, even though I wasn't as utterly crushed by the sadness. It’s like the dark cloud had momentarily moved, but the bizarre world I was experiencing was still very much present. Then the sadness came back, but those other things, the strange thoughts and feelings, they were there all along, for the majority of this whole rough patch, but that period where the mood kind of lifted and the odd experiences continued, that felt really significant.
D005-D007_h018.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h019.question: "It's been a troubling few months, doctor. I preach the Lord's word, and lately, it feels like I'm living a different kind of sermon entirely. There's this woman in the congregation, she looks at me, and I just *know* she's deeply in love with me. It’s an unusual feeling, and despite my conscience, the conviction is strong. And the voices... they're always there, whispering nonsense, fragments of words that make no sense at all. Just last week, I was giving my sermon, and I found myself saying things, words completely jumbled up, nothing connecting. My wife says my face has been like a mask, no joy, no sadness, just... blank. It's tough because I still feel the crushing weight of sadness and hopelessness almost every day. It's been like this for about three months now, with these dark moods lingering for most of that time. But there was a stretch, about three weeks or so, right before the really deep sadness settled in, where I was hearing these voices and certain that woman was in love with me, even though I wasn't feeling particularly down then. I was still coherent enough to go about my duties, but the delusions and voices were definitely present. Then the depressive fog rolled in, and it's been hard to shake since. My usual joy for life, for my ministry, it’s just gone."
D005-D007_h019.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h020.question:
It's been about three months now that things have felt… off. I hear voices, not all the time, but enough that it's unsettling. They mostly tell me I'm destined for something great, that some secret society has chosen me because I have a unique ability to influence minds through my posts. It's exhilarating and terrifying at the same time. Sometimes, when a voice speaks to me, my thoughts just race, jumping from one idea to the next. Other times, I just can't string a coherent sentence together, and I go silent, which is tough for my job as a social media manager.

These last three months have also been incredibly hard. I've been sleeping a lot, crying spells are frequent, and I just can't find joy in anything, even my work, which I used to love. The doctors tell me it's depression, and it feels like it's been with me almost constantly since this all started. But before this major dip, for about two weeks, I was still hearing voices and having those grand thoughts about my special powers, even though my mood was relatively stable. It’s hard to explain, but it’s like the voices and those special feelings were still there, even when the heavy depression wasn't weighing me down as much.
D005-D007_h020.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h021.question: It’s been a really tough few months, almost half a year now. I feel like my world has just… shifted. I’ve been so down, like a heavy blanket is constantly draped over me. Getting out of bed is a monumental task, and the things that used to spark joy in my design work just feel flat and uninteresting. Most days I don’t even have the energy to try. But then there are these other things, these visions, like I’ll see figures in my peripheral vision, shadowy and indistinct, sometimes even a familiar face that quickly dissolves. What's really strange, looking back, is that for a good three weeks, maybe a month even, I was still seeing those shadowy figures and feeling like I was this brilliant innovator, even though that heavy, crushing sadness lifted a little. D005-D007_h022.question:

D005-D007_h023.question:

It’s been a rough few months, doc. Ever since my wife passed, everything just… shifted. I’m 47, and I run the butchery myself, but lately, it’s a struggle to even get out of bed. Most days, I just feel this crushing sadness, like a weight on my chest that never lifts. I’ve lost all interest in everything, even my old fishing spots.

But it's more than just the grief. For about three months now, I've had these strange experiences. I keep smelling this sweet, sickly scent, like rotting meat and lilies – it’s not real, I know it’s not, but it’s always there. And then there’s Mrs. Henderson from next door, she’s been giving me these looks. I’m convinced she’s secretly in love with me; I see the signs, the way she smiles, the way she lingers when she walks by. It’s a bit unsettling, really. Sometimes, when folks are chatting in the shop, I catch myself repeating their last few words without even meaning to.

The strange thing is, even when I have a few better days and the sadness lifts a bit, those smells and the thoughts about Mrs. Henderson, they stick around. Like, for the last two weeks, I haven't felt so down, but the smells and the idea about Mrs. Henderson are still very much there. I just want to feel normal again.
